claim: When a tool door gains new error reason codes, extend every closed reason vocabulary between it and the model in the same change, because a relay that normalizes unrecognized reasons back to unknown erases the protocol-vs-handler distinction the codes were added for.
because: lens-scan execute r-20261014192943-c5dd: a page-bridge fix coded unknown_tool/invalid_arguments/tool_error at the inject door, but the gate and the desktop relay map any reason outside their closed list to unknown, so a re-judge still found the two error channels indistinguishable and the change was reverted.

claim: When a CLI transport port gains an out-of-band result channel (exit code, stderr tail) beside its streamed lines, pin it with a test that spawns a real child through the production transport, because a scripted fake reports the channel by construction and the real adapter can keep reporting the default unnoticed.
because: scan-sweep challenge 2026-10-15: an exit handle and a stderr reader landed with 8 green acceptance cases, all on the scripted transport; the subprocess transport never called report(), so every real run read exit 0 until a real-child test (2 cases red before) drove the fix.

claim: When a host writes a child's input before it reads the child's exit, write it inside the scope that reaps the child and treat a closed or reset pipe as no error, because a child that refuses at startup exits unread and a large input then turns its classified exit and stderr into an unreaped broken-pipe exception.
because: athena-portable 3ef59b4: a 4 MiB stdin to a child that exits 2 without reading raised BrokenPipeError (WinError 109) out of the transport, skipping ADR 0109's exit classification and leaving the child unreaped; after the fix the exit code and stderr tail are reported. No subprocess-lifecycle technique mentions stdin or a broken pipe.

claim: When a canvas or camera binds its keyboard handler on the container, decline any key that is already defaultPrevented, carries Ctrl/Meta/Alt, or targets an editable descendant, because the container hears every key typed inside it and otherwise eats text input, double-handles a child's roving key and swallows the browser's page zoom.
because: cab6dd1: probe showed '-' typed in a field zoomed the camera and never reached the field, a roving list's arrow also orbited, Ctrl+= was prevented; an atlas surface had already worked around it with `event.target !== canvas`

claim: When an overlay's focus restore is deferred to a later frame, resolve the fallback target (and the invoker's connectivity) inside that frame, not at teardown, because the surface beneath can rebuild the landmark between teardown and restore and a teardown-time lookup answers nothing.
because: 26f8424: probe with the origin card re-created by an effect of the closing commit dropped focus to the body; resolving in the frame focused the card

claim: When a state attribute or class toggles a property in CSS, declare the transition on the base selector and let the state rules set values only, because a transition runs on the after-change style, so one declared only on the hidden state animates the exit and pops the enter (and one on a child never fires when the state sets the parent's opacity).
because: atlas lanes: the detail tiers' transition sat only under [data-band=0] and the run's on .al-run-line while data-dim set .al-run; a stylesheet test reading rules (comments stripped) went red on both and green after moving the transitions
